lines.text: Do you know how a car factory builds a car about every minute? Nobody builds a whole car.
The car moves along a line, and each station does one small job. Doors on. Seats in. Wheels on.
Henry Ford tried this in nineteen thirteen. Building a Model T chassis went from about twelve hours to about an hour and a half.
Today, robots do the welding and the painting, and parts arrive right when they're needed.
At the end, every car is tested before it rolls out the door.
Orbi Work runs on the same idea. Type a task, tag a teammate, and it moves step by step. Doing, review, done. And everyone sees it live.
